content.title: About
content.content: Similac for Diarrhea is an infant formula specially designed for children experiencing diarrhea. It provides easily digestible proteins, an optimal electrolyte profile, and pre‑biotics that help restore fluid‑electrolyte balance and normalize gut microbiota.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The formula is enriched with lactulose to promote the growth of beneficial intestinal bacteria.
It contains specific enzymes that aid in lactose breakdown.
Clinically tested in infants with acute diarrhea from 1 month of age.
Packaging includes a water‑contact indicator that changes color for easy preparation.
Available in multiple volumes, from 400 ml to 1 l.

items.title: Restores electrolyte balance
items.content: Contains sodium, potassium, and chloride in ratios similar to breast milk, helping prevent dehydration.

items.title: Supports growth and development
items.content: Provides essential vitamins and minerals (vitamin D, iron, zinc) needed for normal growth even when regular feeding is limited.

items.title: Reduces risk of complications
items.content: Pre‑biotics and probiotics lower the chance of secondary intestinal infections.

items.title: Easy digestion
items.content: Partially hydrolyzed proteins reduce the digestive load.

items.title: Boosts immunity
items.content: Vitamin A and lactobacilli help strengthen immune defenses.

items.title: Milk protein allergy
items.content: Children with confirmed cow‑milk allergy may react to the formula.

items.title: Not a substitute for medical treatment
items.content: Intended as an adjunct; severe diarrhea requires professional medical care.

items.title: Shelf‑life after opening
items.content: Use opened powder within 48 hours and keep it refrigerated.

items.title: Electrolyte overload
items.content: Do not give excessive amounts without physician guidance to avoid hyperkalemia.

content.title: How to Prepare
content.content: Follow the instructions on the package: measure the required amount of powder, add boiled water, cool to 37 °C, and stir until smooth. Do not heat the mixture in a microwave.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the dry powder in its original airtight container in a cool, dry place away from direct sunlight. Prepared formula should be kept in the refrigerator and used within 24 hours.

content.title: About
content.content: Soft gluten‑free pretzels are a baked snack made from gluten‑free flour, usually rice or corn, with a lightly salty flavor and a tender, chewy texture. They are suitable for people with celiac disease and those who prefer a softer pretzel.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Soft pretzels originated in Germany, where they are called "Brezel".
Gluten‑free versions appeared in response to the growing demand for gluten‑free products in the early 2000s.
The dough is leavened with yeast, giving it a puffier crumb than crunchy pretzels.
The coarse salt sprinkled on top is often sea salt, which enhances the flavor.
Soft pretzels are frequently served with dips such as mustard, cheese sauce, or chocolate.

items.title: Gluten‑free
items.content: The absence of gluten makes them safe for individuals with celiac disease or gluten sensitivity.

items.title: Source of carbohydrates
items.content: They provide a quick source of energy thanks to easily digestible carbs.

items.title: Contains iron
items.content: Gluten‑free flour is often fortified with iron, supporting blood formation.

items.title: Provides some fiber
items.content: When whole‑grain gluten‑free flour is used, pretzels can contribute a modest amount of dietary fiber.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Yeast‑leavened dough supplies B‑vitamins that aid metabolism.

items.title: Allergy to ingredients
items.content: Some gluten‑free blends contain soy or dairy proteins that may trigger allergies.

items.title: High glycemic index
items.content: Soft pretzels can raise blood sugar quickly, so they should be eaten in moderation.

items.title: Salt content
items.content: The topping salt may be a concern for people with hypertension.

items.title: Preservatives
items.content: Commercial varieties may contain additives to extend shelf life.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Soft gluten‑free pretzels can be enjoyed as a snack, split and spread with cream cheese, hummus, or nut butter, and served alongside soups and salads.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep in an airtight container at room temperature for up to 3 days. For longer storage, refrigerate up to a week or freeze for up to 2 months.
